newsitem.title: INDIA: Enron submits $10 bln power plan to India - agency.
newsitem.headline: Enron submits $10 bln power plan to India - agency.

text.p: U.S. energy giant Enron Corp has submitted a $10 billion proposal to the Indian government to build power plants able to generate a total 10,000 megawatts of electricity, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Sunday.
The proposal was submitted by Enron Development Corp chief executive Rebecca Mark to Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, the news agency said.
Enron officials could not be reached for comment. A government official confirmed that Mark presented a proposal to the prime minister on Friday, but he could not give any details.

PTI quoted Mark as saying the proposal, under which Enron would share equity stakes in plants with Indian and foreign investors, could be implemented by 2001 if the government cleared it within the next six months.
Enron plans to set up between five and seven power plants, ranging from 1,000 to 2,000 megawatts, in northern India as well as along the coastline in southern states.

The firm proposes using liquefied natural gas (LNG), linking its own gas feed with the state-owned Gas Authority of India's oil and gas pipeline grid across the country, as part of its ambitious plan to meet India's massive electricity shortage.
The total cost of the plan, including the installation of pipelines and gas storage facilities, would be $10 billion, PTI said.
"There was a positive response from the prime minister to the proposal," PTI quoted Mark as saying.
It said preliminary discussions had already been held with officials of some state governments.

"We are not interested in having a majority stake or a controlling stake in the new project but would partner Indian as well as foreign firms picking up a 50 percent equity in each of the ventures," PTI quoted Mark as saying.
Mark said political uncertainties would not hurt Enron's proposed venture.

"Political uncertainties don't bother me anymore. We have been through the worst of times in pushing through the Dabhol project," Mark said, referring to Enron's 2,450-megawatt project in the western state of Maharashtra.
The company said last week that it expected to complete the first phase of the Dabhol power project by December 1998, ahead of an earlier target date of March 1999.
Work on the Dabhol plant resumed late last year after the ruling Hindu nationalist government in Maharashtra renegotiated a contract it had said was too expensive.
The first phase of the $2.3-billion-project will generate 740 megawatts of electricity, Maharashtra government officials said last week.
Negotiations over the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) for the project's 1,440-megawatt second phase would begin by February 25, and be completed by the end of 1997, they said.

Enron's Dabhol Power Company, the firm's local arm, was one of eight fast-track projects designed to lure foreign private investment into India's crumbling infrastructure sector shortly after open market reforms were launched in 1991.
